If * you* felt comfortable attending without a personal invitation, the same expectation applies to others. - **The social media post was the invitation**. Your wife posted a public tribute to your father-in-law at the event location on the correct date. If the missing family saw it (or should have seen it, as they attend annually), they had all the information they needed. ### **2. The " unrepresented" family’s reaction is unreasonable** - They’ve attended *every other year*, so they know the tradition: ** no one individually texts them**. - Claiming they were " * purposely excluded"* is a stretch. If they wanted to attend, they could have: - Checked the family group chat (if one exists). - Seen the social media post (which was public and tagged the event location/date). - Texted your wife or mother-in-law to confirm details (as they’ve done in past years). - **Adults with working phones are responsible for their own attendance**. If they missed the post or assumed they needed a personal invite, that’s on them—not you. ### **3. You’re not the host** - The **mother-in-law** is the one footing the bill and organizing the event. * She* is the de facto " host," not you. - Your role was simply to attend ( which you did, without needing an invite). **You had no obligation to individually reach out to anyone**—especially since the event is " open invitation" by design. - If the missing family felt excluded, they should direct their frustration to the * host* (your mother-in-law), not you. ### **Why this isn’t about " being a good family member"** - ** " Open invitation" events are common in families** (e.g., " all are welcome to the annual reunion at X place on Y date"). - ** " I didn’t get an invite" is the norm for these events**— that’s why they’re called " open invitations." - **If the missing family genuinely didn’t know** ( e.g., they don’t use social media or aren’t in the family group chat), * that* would be a different story. But you said they’ve attended before, so they * know* the process. - **Their anger is misplaced**. They’re treating a * self-organizing* event as if it’s a * private, by- invitation only* gathering. That’s not how " open invitation" works. ### **Final Thought** You did nothing wrong. ** " Open invitation" means " you don’t need a personal invite—you just show up if you can."** The missing family’s expectation of a text message is a misunderstanding of the tradition. If they’re upset, it’s because they’re * not* following the established rules of the event—not because you excluded them. **NTA.** (And if * you* can show up without an invite, so can they. Period.) 💛
